title: decision-path-chronicle-with-rollback-and-cost-signals
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: Create a compact, queryable chronicle format for routing decisions that captures per-hop metrics, rollback triggers, and incremental cost deltas so on-call engineers and SREs can diagnose why a request fell back or why a model variant was selected.

Background: We already capture routing spans and per-hop metrics intermittently, but there is no single-enough artifact that binds: routing policy inputs, tier/region choices, fallback variant substitutions, KV/cache hit context, and the small cost delta associated with each hop. Teams repeatedly ask for a condensed artifact that is cheap to store but rich enough to reproduce and explain regressions and automated rollbacks.

Proposal:
1) Chronicle Frame: define an append-only, line-delimited JSON frame per request containing: timestamped decision events (policy evaluation, model selection, fallback trigger), hop metrics (latency_ms, p50/p95 tokens, cache_hit boolean), and a cost_delta field for the hop. Frames will be compressed with protocol-level dedup keys and optional summarization for low-fidelity retention.
2) Rollback Annotation: attach rollback signals (policy-specified or automatic) to the chronicle with rationale tags (e.g., model_ver, region, metric_reason="latency_slo_breach") and a snapshot reference to the evaluation prompt set when available.
3) Sampling & Retention: default adaptive sampling that keeps 100% of high-impact events (fallbacks where customer_impact != none, SLO breach, or canary rollouts), and 1% for routine decisions. Retention tiers: 7 days (full fidelity), 90 days (summarized).
4) Query ergonomics: provide a simple API to request a chronicle bundle by request_id, or to search by model_variant, region, rollback_reason, and cost_delta ranges. Expose a console view which renders the chronicle as a timeline with per-hop expandable frames.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema defined and reviewed by infra and privacy (1.21 doc).
- Server-side serializer implemented in routing-service with <5% added p50 latency for sampled requests.
- Storage pipeline: streaming to observability Kafka topic, processing job creates summaries and writes chronicle frames to S3 and metadata to trace index.
- Console: timeline view prototype that displays up to 20 hops with cost deltas, region/tier badges, and rollback rationale.

Trade-offs considered:
- Fidelity vs. cost: per-hop token-level traces would be too expensive; we capture aggregates and attach sampled full-context snapshots only when triggered.
- Privacy/PII: snapshotting is opt-in per-tenant; default is redaction. We will coordinate with security for KMS keys for stored snapshots.

Open questions:
- Should cost_delta be normalized to a canonical unit (tokens * unit_cost) or captured as provider-reported compute_ms? (We'll prototype both.)
- Indexing strategy: make chronicle ID the primary lookup versus adding secondary indexes for model_variant queries.

Links: Confluence design doc, prototype dashboard, and prototype PRs are referenced in the comments below.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Scoped initial design. Met with PM (Ava Martinez) and SRE to align on storage budget and sampling thresholds. Action: produce schema proposal and sample chronicle serialization.

2026-03-11 — Design review: feedback from infra (Rajiv) to avoid per-request writes to the trace index; suggested buffered batch writes and a lightweight metadata envelope for fast lookup. Updated schema to include envelope_id and compressed_payload_ref. Added edge-case for multi-region fanout.

2026-03-12 — Implementation started: routing-service serializer prototype in feature/chronicle-serializer branch. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/3922 — includes unit tests for frame inflation and compression.

2026-03-12 — QA note: local benchmarking shows 3% p50 latency increase on sampled requests with gzip compression; investigating switch to zstd level 1. Also verifying that retention summarizer job can run in <2s per 10k frames.
2026-03-13 — PM review (Ava): approved sampling policy for canaries and SLO breaches; asked to add console UX mockups for the timeline zoom behavior. Design to provide mockups by 2026-03-16.
